subject: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Subject: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request

Team — quick ask. Zelos (large digital health customer) just moved to signature but they have two non-negotiable asks in their SOW that we need prioritized to meet the go-live on 2028-07-15: 1) conditional routing rules that allow per-request routing to a pinned model variant based on request metadata (region + regulatory flag), and 2) tenant-level pinning so a subset of their traffic stays on a higher-capacity residency pool (warm lanes) for compliance SLA.

Why this matters: they are committing to a 12-month reserved capacity contract (~$1.4M ARR) but have a firm go-live date and regulatory checks tied to residency/route guarantees. If we miss the feature window they will push the launch and potentially reduce committed capacity.

Ask: can eng/product provide realistic scope and a prioritization slot? Zelos is willing to pre-pay a portion of the first quarter and sign a timed acceptance milestone if we can commit to the July window. Attached SOW + PRD summary.

High-level constraints: minimal latency regression (+/-10ms), prefer config-driven rules (no heavy infra changes). Happy to trade phased delivery: routing first, then full warm-lane pinning.

Next step: Dev/Jonas/Karthik — can you respond with: a) feasible delivery approach b) estimated dev + QA effort (sprint count) c) blocker list by EOD 6/8 so I can update Zelos and procurement.

Thanks — Soojin
---
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request

Thanks Soojin — quick technical clarifications before we estimate:
1) Conditional routing: do they expect rules evaluated synchronously per-request (decision in the hot path) or an edge-router decision with async re-routing? Synchronous has latency implications; we can implement a lightweight decision layer but need to bound rule complexity.
2) Tenant pinning: is this affinity for a warm-pool instance (residency + pin) or model variant pin (quantized vs fp16)? Confirm which.

From reading the SOW: sounds like region + a compliance flag -> pinned residency. If so, we will need: schema for metadata header, router extension, warm-pool reservation API + billing tagging, and rollout hooks. Rough estimate ballpark (very rough) for a narrow MVP: 3 sprints backend + 1 sprint infra/ops for warm lanes + 1 sprint for QA and docs — total ~5 sprints (~10 weeks). This assumes we can reuse the existing warm-pool machinery and just add pinning tag + routing rule evaluator.

Blockers: cross-region capacity availability for their region (eu-west), KMS/CMK verification for pinned pool audit logs, and acceptance criteria for perf regression.

I will dig into the router code and confirm effort tomorrow.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-08T09:45:00-07:00
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request

On Thu, Jun 7, 2028 at 11:03 AM Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Soojin — quick technical clarifications before we estimate:
> 1) Conditional routing: do they expect rules evaluated synchronously per-request (decision in the hot path) or an edge-router decision with async re-routing?

We discussed this in infra sync — engineering preference is an in-proxy decision that's fast (synchronous evaluation of a limited rule set). That keeps implementation surface small and keeps routing deterministic. Implementation sketch: add a small policy evaluator (lua-like or mini-dsl) to the request router that can match metadata headers -> route to pinned pool or default.

For tenant pinning (as described in the SOW): they want residency-affinity to a higher-capacity warm pool for a percentage of traffic + an always-on set of request types. This requires: tagging in the scheduler, reservation API in the warm-pool manager, and verification hooks in telemetry to prove routing guarantees.

Estimate (refined from Dev): MVP scope if prioritized immediately:
- Router policy evaluator + API for rules: 2 sprints
- Warm-pool reservation + tagging + billing hook: 2 sprints
- Telemetry + acceptance test harness (traceable routing asserts): 1 sprint
- Docs + rollout automation: 1 sprint
Total: 6 sprints (~12 weeks). If we do a phased approach (router-only + manual warm-pool provisioning), we can cut to 4 sprints and unblock Zelos earlier.

Constraints/risks:
- Capacity in eu-west: we need ops confirmation this week
- KMS/CMK audit path for pinned residency logs (security needs to sign off)
- Perf: router policy must be <5ms additional p50 to meet their SLA

If Sales can accept a phased rollout (phase 1 router + manual warm pool), we can commit to July gating for a constrained subset. Full automated pinning by Sep.

— Jonas
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-08T13:02:00-07:00
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ellen Park <ellen@zelos.ai>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@zelos.ai>
Subject: Re: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request

Appreciate the breakdown — thanks Jonas and Dev. Zelos is agreeable to a phased approach. They will accept phase 1 that includes: synchronous router policy (region + compliance flag) and a manual warm-pool standby for pinned traffic limited to 20% of requests. Acceptance test will be a traceable sample showing pinned requests consistently hitting the warm pool. They want phase 1 in place for the July 15 go-live; full automation (reservation API + billing) can come in phase 2 with a Sept milestone.

Attached updated SOW reflecting phased acceptance. Procurement (procurement@zelos.ai) will expedite partial pre-payment if we sign off on the July milestone.

Soojin — I'll flag to Marissa that this is mission-critical for the deal. Need product sign-off on phased acceptance criteria and eng allocation confirmation.

— Soojin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-09T10:20:00-07:00
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request

Thanks for the clear options. From GTM perspective we should prioritize Phase 1 into the next prioritization window. Zelos is strategic for our healthcare vertical and the ARR is material. My asks:
- Product sign-off on the acceptance test definition (simple traceable routing evidence + perf gates)
- If eng can commit to the phased plan and the 4-sprint fast-path, Sales will accept the July 15 go-live and ask procurement to release the pre-pay.

I authorize Sales to offer Zelos a short-term operational workaround (manual warm-pool assignment) during the July launch if Eng needs more time to ship the reservation API. But that operational cost should be recorded and billed back to the deal as an activation service line.

Please confirm by EOD so I can approve PO release.

— Marissa
VP Sales, Enterprise
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-09T16:30:00-07:00
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@zelos.ai
Subject: Re: Zelos activation: conditional routing + tenant pin prioritization request

Okay — product accepts the phased approach and signs off on the acceptance criteria below: 
1) Router policy evaluator supports match on headers: region and compliance_flag, returns route tag (pinned|default).
2) P50 latency of policy evaluation + routing hop <5ms in canary traffic.
3) Manual warm-pool assignment documented and runbooked; telemetry shows >95% of pinned-tagged requests hitting the warm pool in a 10k-sample trace.

We can deliver the fast-path (router + manual warm pool) in 4 sprints if we get an immediate prioritization slot and ops confirms capacity. I'll raise an execution ticket and assign owners: Dev (router evaluator + policy API), Jonas (warm-pool ops integration), Karthik (acceptance tests + docs).

Dev/Jonas — please create the JIRA epic today and tag it 'ZEL-Activation'. Sales — share the signed SOW and PO link once available.

Karthik
PM, Routing & Resiliency
